affiliations.date_precision: A 1960 newspaper places Library employment after his 1939 graduation and before Army service; a November 1942 journal issue gives the same affiliation.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Newton Miler is confirmed as Newton Scott Miler in a direct federal OSS/SSU personnel file.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The indexed name, official file title, full name in the application, and SSU candidate sheet identify the same person.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through a direct named personnel file linked to the indexed spelling.
claims.temporal_assessment: The file concerns a 1946 SSU candidacy after wartime OSS; the distinction is preserved.
claims.match_notes: No irrelevant personal details or full service identifier are published.

claims.claim_text: Immediately before his 1946 SSU candidacy, Miler was a student at Dartmouth College.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: His application and admission sheet both describe continuing student status when SSU considered him.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person through the direct personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly current in August 1946; this is immediate pre-SSU status, not a wartime OSS employer.
claims.match_notes: Dartmouth is classified as an educational institution and student relationship, not an employer.

claims.claim_text: Miler served in the Navy's V-12 and NROTC program at Dartmouth from 1 March 1944 to 1 July 1946.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The federal application supplies the program, institution, and exact dates.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person through the direct personnel file.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded military training that ended shortly before the SSU application.
claims.match_notes: Military training is separated from both student status and civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: At SSU admission in August 1946, Miler described himself as unemployed while still attending school.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The candidate admission sheet explicitly records this status.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person through the direct personnel file.
claims.match_notes: This does not mean he had never worked; the application mentions unnamed brief store jobs that cannot support a named employer claim.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Milton E. Miles is a high-confidence match to career naval officer Milton Edward Miles.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The distinctive exact name and middle initial align with an official Navy biography documenting his wartime China intelligence command.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from distinctive name agreement and a highly specific official wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Navy biography supplies continuous service chronology; it does not state an OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The indexed row lacks rank, so rank is not silently inserted into the source transcription.

claims.claim_text: Miles served as Member and Recorder of the Navy Department Interior Control Board immediately before his 1942 China command.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official Navy biography dates the board assignment through March 1942 and the China command from 4 May 1942.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive-name match to the indexed person.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded predecessor assignment; the source does not define a formal OSS transfer.
claims.match_notes: Published as a military assignment, not a civilian employer, and qualified to the China command represented by the indexed file.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Lloyd S. Millegan is a high-confidence match to the Library of Congress employee who later served in the wartime Army.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact name and initial align across the index, a contemporary scholarly byline, and a newspaper chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from a distinctive exact name and mutually consistent institutional and wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources establish pre-Army Library employment; the exact OSS entry date remains unknown.
claims.match_notes: Later Pacific Army service is used for identity context, not as a pre-OSS employer.

claims.claim_text: Millegan's best-supported last civilian employer before wartime Army service was the Library of Congress.
claims.evidence_excerpt: employed in Washington, D. C., at the Library of Congress
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A retrospective newspaper chronology places the employment after 1939 graduation and before Army service; a 1942 journal gives the same affiliation.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High-confidence distinctive-name match supported by two independent reputable sources.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded as the last named civilian employer before Army service; immediate OSS succession is not proven.
claims.match_notes: The claim is limited to last civilian employer before military service and does not assert direct Library-to-OSS recruitment.

claims.claim_text: Indexed Lieutenant George Milkovich is confirmed by a direct contemporary OSS personnel report.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The report agrees in exact name, officer grade, protected identifier, Army chronology, and OSS Operational Group assignment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed through a direct contemporary OSS record and privately reviewed protected-identifier agreement.
claims.temporal_assessment: The report explicitly dates Army entry, commissioning, and OSS assignment.
claims.match_notes: The full protected identifier is excluded from public output.

claims.claim_text: Milkovich entered the Army in December 1942, was commissioned in May 1943, and was assigned to OSS on 10 August 1943.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A direct OSS report supplies the complete Army-to-OSS sequence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person through the same direct record and private identifier agreement.
claims.match_notes: Army service is not labeled civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: Before Army service, Milkovich's documented civilian occupation was mechanical engineer.
claims.evidence_excerpt: In civilian life was a mechanical engineer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The contemporary OSS report names the occupation but no company.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed exact person through the direct OSS record.
claims.temporal_assessment: Explicitly described as his civilian-life occupation before Army and OSS service; employer and dates are unstated.
claims.match_notes: Occupation-only finding; no engineering employer is invented.
